claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 can be produced as an amorphous alloy by rapid quenching.
Slower cooling of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 produces a complex multiphase crystalline structure.
The rapidly quenched amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy is prone to crystallization during later thermal exposure.
A brief electric arc pulse reheat applied immediately after rapid quenching will increase amorphous retention in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
A brief electric arc pulse reheat applied immediately after rapid quenching will increase the thermal stability of amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The pulse reheat will promote nonequilibrium chemical short-range order in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Enhanced nonequilibrium chemical short-range order reduces the number of nucleation sites for primary crystallization.
Limited atomic mobility during the short reheat permits relaxation into a more stable amorphous network.
The resulting short-range-ordered amorphous network kinetically inhibits nucleation and growth of primary crystalline phases during subsequent reheating.
Rapid quenching of this alloy occurs at approximately 10^5–10^6 K/s.
Approximately 1340 K is an appropriate intermediate pulse-reheat temperature below the conventional FCC crystallization temperature of this alloy.
The conventional crystallization boundary relevant to the intervention is approximately 1706 K.
Relative to rapid quenching alone, pulse-reheated samples will retain a larger amorphous phase fraction.
Relative to rapid quenching alone, pulse-reheated samples will exhibit a delayed crystallization onset during subsequent thermal analysis.
Exceeding the proposed pulse-temperature or pulse-duration window could trigger bulk crystallization and eliminate the stabilization benefit.

contradictions.description: The initial-state and baseline fields distinguish amorphous rapidly quenched material from multiphase slowly cooled material, but the predicted-outcome wording can be read as saying that both rapid-quench-only and slower-cooled samples exhibit multiple non-eutectic crystalline phases.
